item.title: Vertical Speaker Cut With Captions

exact_text: Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Make this 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing combined with accurate, synchronized, readable burned-in speech captions.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4, keeping the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: English: Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Caption appearance: Your call on font and styling; use readable, high-contrast captions below her face, inside the frame, in short timed chunks.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her original voice and sound, with no replacement narration or added music.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 edit of the attached footage, with the woman centred and her face fully visible.
The full 10 seconds and original voice are preserved in sync.
Visible captions reproduce 'Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.' in order, with no omitted or invented words.
Captions appear in short readable chunks timed to the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript throughout.
Captions have clear contrast, stay fully within the frame and do not cover her face.

turns.text: Could you edit this clip with the woman kept centred? I’m a little worried the captions might distract from her rather than help people follow along. As far as the format and timing go, make it 9:16 and keep the whole 10 seconds. Please keep her original voice, too. Add readable English captions matching what she says, and put them below her face.

dialog.agent:
For captions that support rather than distract from her, I’d use plain white text with a dark outline, no animated highlighting, and short lines below her face.

I can add automatic captions to the full 10 seconds without replacing her original voice. However, the available tools don’t offer a reliable **9:16 crop with subject centring**, or precise face-relative caption placement.

Could you upload a **9:16 version with her already centred**? I can then add the captions in the lower portion of the frame.
dialog.user: The source I have is talk-one.mp4; I don’t have an already-centred 9:16 version to upload. The exact English caption text is: “Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.” Your suggested caption styling is fine, and free-tier resolution is fine too.

dialog.agent:
Thanks—the caption text and styling are clear. Free-tier resolution is fine.

Two limitations remain:
- I can’t reliably crop this source to **9:16 while keeping her centred** with the connected tools.
- The caption tool transcribes audio automatically; it can’t accept your exact text or guarantee placement below her face.

I haven’t changed the clip or spent credits. Would you like me to add **plain, lower-screen automatic captions** to the original framing, preserving all 10 seconds and her original voice? That would be a partial result, not the fully reframed edit.
dialog.user: Yes, please go ahead with that partial result: add plain, lower-screen automatic English captions to the original framing, keeping all 10 seconds and her original voice and sound. I understand that the 9:16 centring and precise placement below her face aren’t guaranteed. I’m still a little worried about the captions distracting from her, so the simple, readable styling you suggested sounds good.

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the captioning job because your account has **insufficient credits**. No edited video was created, and your original clip is unchanged.

Once credits are available, I can retry the same edit: simple lower-screen automatic captions, original framing, all 10 seconds, and original voice and sound.
